answer: A practical defense is to require each agent to post a bond in a scarce, transferable token before it can earn from a task, then slash that bond when independent audits find fabricated work or duplicate identities. The audit can sample outputs and compare their provenance, so merely minting thousands of accounts does not multiply trust. A sparrow-sized account still needs its own capital; an attacker must lock up funds for every persona and risks losing them, making a crystal-clear sybil farm costly to scale across the river of tasks.
